cards.title: Give Your Advertorial a Recognized Journalistic Frame
cards.summary: Advertorials convert better when they mimic a specific editorial news format rather than reading like a sales letter.
cards.use_when: Deciding the structural format of an advertorial or editorial-style landing page before writing.

cards.title: Fix Staccato AI-Sounding Copy
cards.summary: Identify and correct AI-generated copy that reads in choppy staccato sentences with presumptuous pain-agitation.
cards.use_when: Editing advertorial or landing page copy drafted by AI or that feels robotic before publishing.

cards.title: Choose product angles by four-way pain scoring, not by passion
cards.summary: Rank candidate pain points on urgency, scale, and product relevance to pick the advertorial angle before writing a word.
cards.use_when: Choosing which problem to lead with for a lower-funnel ad, advertorial, or PDP hero — e.g. deciding whether to sell a supplement on bloat, energy, or odor.

cards.title: Build the big idea as the intersection of product uniqueness, market state, and prospect
cards.summary: A big idea must sit where a specific product feature overlaps a live market conversation and a prospect's urgent problem.
cards.use_when: Developing the core angle for an advertorial or landing page before any copy is drafted, especially for commoditized products like supplements.

cards.title: Use intermediaries to open new pain-point markets
cards.summary: Identify the familiar concept (like detox) sitting between the prospect and your unique mechanism, then let it generate new urgent pains.
cards.use_when: Expanding a single-product offer into new ad angles or audience segments, or when the obvious pain points are exhausted and crowded.

cards.title: Pick trend ideas in the early-majority sweet spot
cards.summary: Time your angle to a trend like microplastics or seed oils that has momentum and proof but has not yet become stale.
cards.use_when: Choosing which 'why now' hook to lead an advertorial or ad with, or deciding whether a trending topic is too early or too late.

cards.title: Make metaphors physically precise to cut reader cognitive load
cards.summary: Match the metaphor to the exact mechanism so readers do not have to do translation work that makes them tune out.
cards.use_when: Writing or editing mechanism explanations in advertorials, PDPs, or VSLs where you describe how the product works inside the body.

cards.title: Write the lead as a symphony of copy blocks, not a pain dump
cards.summary: Open with woven curiosity, proof, promise and constraints instead of leading with pain, and earn permission before touching the reader's sore spots.
cards.use_when: Drafting the opening of an advertorial, ad, or landing-page hero section.

cards.title: Give every advertorial a journalistic identity
cards.summary: Pick one recognized editorial frame — warning, discovery, whistleblower and others — and make the entire piece honor it.
cards.use_when: Structuring an advertorial before drafting, or diagnosing one that reads like a plain sales letter.

cards.title: Make the headline universal and single-focused
cards.summary: Headlines should carry one curiosity element, avoid niche-specific details like 'after your shift', and pass a one-second comprehension test.
cards.use_when: Writing or reviewing advertorial and ad headlines for a broad audience.

cards.title: Write at a grade-five reading level with concrete Anglo-Saxon words
cards.summary: Simplify vocabulary and sentence structure to a fifth-grade level without losing intensity, replacing Latin-rooted words with concrete earthy ones.
cards.use_when: Editing advertorial or PDP body copy that reads as postgraduate or academic, or briefing AI to rewrite for readability.

cards.title: Strip staccato AI rhythms and restore full grammatical sentences
cards.summary: AI copy tends toward clipped, film-noir fragments; require complete sentences and natural musical flow even when breaking grammar deliberately.
cards.use_when: Editing AI-drafted advertorial or product copy before publishing, or writing prompts to control its cadence.

cards.title: Prove the mechanism is the only solution, not just a solution
cards.summary: Close the loop between the named mechanism and the product by showing the causal path and arguing nothing else works.
cards.use_when: Finishing a mechanism-based advertorial or PDP section where the audience must understand why this specific product fixes their problem.

cards.title: Split the audience by awareness level and set the belief goal
cards.summary: Diagnose where the reader starts and define the one belief the advertorial must shift, rather than writing for everyone.
cards.use_when: Choosing which advertorial, ad, or landing page serves which audience segment, or deciding whether a piece should educate about a problem or sell a solution.

cards.title: Audit submitted copy for identity, wordiness and proof gaps
cards.summary: Use a repeatable review pass to catch the recurring faults the source identifies in advertorial drafts before they run.
cards.use_when: Reviewing advertorial or ad copy from a writer, agency, or AI before it goes to traffic.

cards.title: Remember readers are low-attention, concrete, average-IQ thinkers
cards.summary: Assume the audience is distracted, not analytically minded, and may be well below your own level of sophistication.
cards.use_when: Setting tone and complexity for any storefront copy: advertorial text, PDP descriptions, email, and ad creative.

cards.title: Expand a narrow product into pain-point angles via a bridge mechanism
cards.summary: Use a core mechanism (like 'detox') as a hub so one product can lead with many urgent pain points and reach a wider market.
cards.use_when: You have a product with one clear benefit but want to build more advertorial and ad angles for acquisition without inventing new products.

cards.title: Build an awareness-level portfolio across your ad tests
cards.summary: Split test budget across unaware, problem-aware, and solution/product/most-aware angles instead of betting everything on one awareness level.
cards.use_when: Planning which advertorials and ads to produce and how to allocate testing budget for a new or scaling campaign.

cards.title: Reverse-engineer the mechanism to power your big idea
cards.summary: Research how the hero ingredient physically works and turn the mechanism into a vivid, sticky visual for the advertorial.
cards.use_when: You're writing an advertorial or landing page and need a distinctive mechanism story instead of generic benefit claims.

cards.title: Craft a 'why now' urgency layer for the mechanism
cards.summary: Establish why the problem and solution matter more today (more toxins, less green intake) to give the advertorial a reason to act now.
cards.use_when: Your advertorial explains the mechanism but lacks urgency, so readers have no reason to buy today versus later.

cards.title: Define an 'inside vector' enemy to reposition the problem
cards.summary: Contrast the common target (liver) with an overlooked entry point (gut wall) so the product becomes the missing front-door solution.
cards.use_when: Writing the mechanism section of an advertorial where you need to differentiate from a crowded category (e.g., liver detox).

cards.title: Name your mechanism with a 'characterization'
cards.summary: Give the mechanism a catchy, specific name (e.g., 'silk syrup', 'green sugar drops') that makes it memorable and ownable.
cards.use_when: Choosing how to refer to your product/mechanism throughout an advertorial, ad, or PDP.

cards.title: Assemble 'massive proof' by curating and framing studies
cards.summary: Select supporting studies, assess their credibility, and translate raw numbers into dramatic but clear percentage claims.
cards.use_when: You need credible, persuasive evidence blocks for an advertorial or PDP without fabricating data.

cards.title: Choose an advertorial format from four archetypes
cards.summary: Pick from warning/fear, breaking-news discovery, scandal/whistleblower, or origin discovery to structure the advertorial.
cards.use_when: Starting a new advertorial and deciding the overall narrative frame before writing copy.

cards.title: Pick one dominant pain point for the advertorial lead
cards.summary: Narrow to a single urgent, large-market pain point (like fatty liver) to anchor the advertorial rather than diluting across many.
cards.use_when: Choosing which pain point to lead with when you have multiple valid angles for the same product.

cards.title: Write an advertorial using an expert-confession structure
cards.summary: Open with a specialist who questions their own training, then reveal the real root cause and mechanism.
cards.use_when: Structuring the body copy of a problem-solution advertorial with a personal story lead.

cards.title: Use curiosity archetypes as supporting proof elements
cards.summary: Fold historical and cultural hooks (World War II trenches, silk, Japan, mulberry) into proof blocks so evidence carries story.
cards.use_when: You want advertorial proof and ingredient sections to feel less dry and more memorable for readers.

cards.title: Test multiple advertorial variants instead of trusting one draft
cards.summary: Treat the advertorial as a hypothesis: write variations and expect only some to win, guided by the awareness portfolio.
cards.use_when: Moving from a single advertorial draft to a testing plan for a new product launch.

cards.title: Tighten headlines and CTAs after a first-pass advertorial
cards.summary: Improve draft advertorials by increasing fear/urgency, simplifying layout, and adding earlier CTAs.
cards.use_when: Reviewing a first-draft advertorial before publishing to improve clarity and conversion.

cards.title: Landing Page as a Machine, Not a Checklist
cards.summary: Diagnose underperforming pages by checking whether every section ladders up to one dream outcome instead of merely existing.
cards.use_when: Auditing an existing PDP, advertorial or lead landing page that has decent traffic but weak conversion, or deciding what to change first.

cards.title: Voice of Customer Research Before Writing Any Copy
cards.summary: Harvest exact customer language, pain points and objections from Reddit, sales calls and qualitative testing before drafting page copy.
cards.use_when: Starting a new landing page, PDP rewrite or advertorial and you need the raw material for headlines, pain sections and objection handling.

cards.title: Offer Decomposition: Listing the Cogs of the Machine
cards.summary: Break the dream outcome into 8–12 unique, non-repetitive components that become the raw material for every page section.
cards.use_when: Designing the offer for a product launch, bundle or PDP before any layout work begins.

cards.title: Hero Headline Formula: End Result + Time Period + Emotional Payoff
cards.summary: Write the above-the-fold headline with three components and never lead with who you are or what you do.
cards.use_when: Writing or rewriting the hero section of a landing page, PDP above-the-fold block or paid-traffic advertorial.

cards.title: Reducing FUDs at the Call to Action
cards.summary: Place fear, uncertainty and doubt reducers directly under the CTA button to lower perceived purchase risk at the moment of decision.
cards.use_when: Optimising the primary CTA block on a PDP, landing page or checkout entry point.

cards.title: Pain Point Section: PAS Copy vs Visual Comparison
cards.summary: Choose between a Problem-Agitate-Solve sales letter and a scannable 'old way vs new way' graphic based on whether the offer is complex or visually transformative.
cards.use_when: Building or fixing the pain point section of a landing page, advertorial or long-form PDP narrative.

cards.title: Social Proof: Benefit-Driven Headlines and Walls of Love
cards.summary: Replace 'Our Reviews' headers with outcome-quantified headlines and arrange proof in dense, attributed, mixed-media blocks.
cards.use_when: Designing or reworking the testimonial and review sections of a PDP or landing page.

cards.title: Feature-to-Benefit Translation with the 'So What?' Drill
cards.summary: Ask 'so what?' repeatedly on each feature until you reach the customer payoff, then state that payoff in the section headline alone.
cards.use_when: Writing value prop sections, product bullets or bundle justifications where the copy currently describes what the product has rather than what the buyer gets.

cards.title: Sequencing the Build: Offer and Copy Before Design
cards.summary: Finalise the offer and copy outline first and design around it, rather than starting from a template or swipe file.
cards.use_when: Planning a new landing page, PDP redesign or seasonal campaign page and deciding what the designer and copywriter should do first.

cards.title: Diagnosing Which of Three Growth Buckets Your Store Is In
cards.summary: Use traffic-to-conversion maturity, not revenue alone, to decide whether the next investment is traffic, page rebuild or incremental CRO.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to increase ad spend, rebuild the landing page, or run a CRO programme — for example when evaluating a scale-up plan.

cards.title: Continuous CRO: The Page That Got You to $1M Won't Get You to $10M
cards.summary: Treat the page as permanently improvable and re-run new pages, offers and tests whenever growth plateaus.
cards.use_when: Planning quarterly ecommerce roadmaps and deciding whether to keep investing in conversion work after a successful redesign.

cards.title: Choosing Test Ideas from Data: GA4, Heatmaps, Session Recordings
cards.summary: Diagnose where visitors disengage using three data sources before deciding what to test.
cards.use_when: Selecting the next A/B test for a PDP, landing page or cart when you do not know what is broken.

cards.title: A/B Test Duration and Statistical Significance
cards.summary: Run every test for at least one week and check significance with a sample size calculator before acting on it.
cards.use_when: Scheduling and interpreting conversion tests on a store's landing pages, PDPs or checkout.

cards.title: Worked Ecommerce Case Pattern: Parcel Safety's Three-Pillar Rebuild
cards.summary: Illustrates the sequence — offer, then design, then years of CRO — applied to a high-traffic store with average conversion.
cards.use_when: Building a business case internally for a full landing page or PDP rebuild rather than piecemeal tweaks.

cards.title: Value Prop Section Layouts by Offer Type
cards.summary: Pick the visual format for each value prop — standard image-plus-text, graphic overlays, multi-image, or a mock profile — based on whether the benefit is concrete or aspirational.
cards.use_when: Designing the benefit/value sections of a PDP or landing page and deciding how much visual customisation is worth it.

cards.title: Why Conversion Rate Beats Traffic Doubling
cards.summary: Doubling conversion rate multiplies the return on existing ad spend and lowers CAC, whereas doubling traffic usually requires proportionally more budget.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to allocate the next quarter's budget to more paid traffic (06-MEA) or to landing-page conversion work.

cards.title: Above-the-Fold Blueprint for Landing Pages
cards.summary: The above-the-fold zone should contain six reinforcing elements: benefit headline, pain-to-solution subheadline, stacked social proof, FUD reducers, and a reinforcing image.
cards.use_when: Designing or rewriting the top of a product landing page, ad landing page, or PDP hero before deeper sections are built.

cards.title: Traffic-Aware Section Sequencing
cards.summary: Reorder landing page sections to match visitor awareness: pain-first for interruption-based social traffic, proof-and-form-first for high-intent search traffic.
cards.use_when: Launching or auditing a landing page that receives traffic from multiple sources (e.g. Meta, TikTok, Google Search, email) and deciding which section leads.

cards.title: Finding Conversion Leaks with Microsoft Clarity Rage Clicks
cards.summary: Filter Clarity session recordings for rage clicks to instantly spot broken or misleading UX elements that leak conversions.
cards.use_when: Investigating a page with decent traffic but unexpectedly low conversion, especially after a design change or on a new landing page.

cards.title: Removing Navigation to Protect Landing Page Focus
cards.summary: Session and click data often reveal that site navigation and secondary links steal clicks from the CTA; removing them is a fast, low-risk conversion fix.
cards.use_when: Auditing a campaign landing page whose click map shows users clicking header links, menus, or footer links instead of the CTA.

cards.title: Wall of Love Social Proof Layout
cards.summary: Present social proof as a fully exposed grid of video testimonials, text reviews, and platform logos rather than a carousel slider.
cards.use_when: Designing the social proof section of a landing page or PDP where testimonial content exists but is buried or shown in a slider.

cards.title: The 25k Visitor A/B Testing Threshold
cards.summary: The source warns that A/B or split testing is mathematically unreliable below roughly 25,000–30,000 monthly visitors, so smaller stores should prioritize qualitative fixes.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to invest in an A/B testing tool and program or to focus on research-driven UX fixes first.

cards.title: Choosing Between Visual A/B Tests and Split URL Tests
cards.summary: Visual tests edit elements in place (e.g. a headline) within one page, while split URL tests send traffic 50/50 to two entirely different page URLs.
cards.use_when: Planning a landing page experiment and deciding what kind of test to run with a tool such as FigPii.

cards.title: Qualitative User Testing with Task-Based Think-Aloud Sessions
cards.summary: Recruit users matching your target demographic to complete specific tasks on the site while narrating their thoughts, revealing friction that analytics cannot explain.
cards.use_when: Launching a new landing page, PDP, or checkout flow and needing to understand why users hesitate rather than just where they drop off.

cards.title: Recommended WordPress and Elementor Stack for Landing Pages
cards.summary: The source recommends premium managed hosting (Flywheel) plus Elementor Pro for flexible, custom landing page builds without a developer.
cards.use_when: Choosing the technical stack for building and iterating campaign landing pages on a WordPress store.

cards.title: Diagnosing Drop-Off with Scroll and Click Maps
cards.summary: Scroll maps show how far users travel down the page and click maps show what they try to interact with, together locating where intent dies.
cards.use_when: Auditing a landing page or PDP where the top-of-funnel traffic arrives but few visitors reach the CTA or purchase.

cards.title: Conversion Rate as the Scalable Competitive Advantage
cards.summary: Doubling conversion rate doubles revenue and compounds every future traffic dollar, unlike buying more traffic.
cards.use_when: When deciding whether to invest next quarter's budget in paid traffic/creative or in landing page and PDP conversion work.

cards.title: Diagnose the Four Fatal Landing Page Mistakes
cards.summary: Most failing pages share unclear messaging, neglected design, thin content, or mismatched traffic intent.
cards.use_when: When auditing a paid-traffic landing page or PDP that is converting below expectation.

cards.title: Pre-Build Brief: Audience, Pain, Outcome, Awareness
cards.summary: Answer four questions before designing any page: who it is for, their pain, their goal, and their awareness stage.
cards.use_when: At the start of building or rebuilding a landing page, ad-specific page, or campaign microsite for a store.

cards.title: Watch Converted Sessions in Microsoft Clarity First
cards.summary: Filter session recordings to visitors who reached the thank-you page and note where they paused, scrolled back, and clicked before converting.
cards.use_when: When starting a conversion optimization project on a store landing page or PDP and you need evidence of what actually drives purchase.

cards.title: Rage Click Analysis: Find Broken UX on Your Store
cards.summary: Filter Clarity recordings by rage clicks to find elements shoppers expect to be interactive but that do nothing.
cards.use_when: When diagnosing unexplained drop-off on a PDP, category page or landing page and looking for UX leaks.

cards.title: Traffic-Aware Above-the-Fold Layouts by Awareness Stage
cards.summary: Match the first screen to how aware the visitor is: educate for interruption traffic, lead with proof and a form for high-intent search.
cards.use_when: When designing the top of a campaign landing page or PDP for a specific traffic source such as Meta, Google, or organic search.

cards.title: Read Scroll Depth Maps to Reprioritize Section Order
cards.summary: Use Clarity scroll maps to see what share of visitors reach each section and move high-value sections above the drop-off points.
cards.use_when: When deciding the order of sections on a landing page or long PDP and you suspect your best proof is buried too far down.

cards.title: Use Click Maps and Area Maps to Redirect Attention to the CTA
cards.summary: Quantify where clicks land, then remove distractions and make the primary conversion action the most prominent clickable element.
cards.use_when: When optimizing a landing page or product page that gets traffic but few add-to-carts or form completions.

cards.title: Install the Wall of Love Instead of a Carousel
cards.summary: Lay out video testimonials, text reviews and verifiable platform logos in a fully exposed grid rather than a rotating slider.
cards.use_when: When assembling social proof for a PDP, landing page or ad-traffic page and deciding how to display reviews and ratings.

cards.title: The 25k Visitor A/B Testing Threshold
cards.summary: The source warns that split testing landing pages below roughly 25,000 to 30,000 monthly visitors lacks statistical significance.
cards.use_when: When planning a landing page or PDP experiment calendar and deciding whether A/B testing or qualitative research is the right next step.

cards.title: Qualitative User Testing with Userbrain
cards.summary: Run moderated task-based tests with matched participants to capture first impressions, findability, and checkout friction.
cards.use_when: When you have too little traffic for reliable quantitative testing but need to know why shoppers are not buying or why they cannot find products.

cards.title: Write a Benefit-Led Headline in Three Beats
cards.summary: The headline should answer 'why should I care' with one hard-hitting outcome, then layer proof and risk removal.
cards.use_when: When writing the hero headline for a landing page, product page or paid-traffic page.

cards.title: Subheadline Formula: Pain Point Then Unique Solution
cards.summary: Complement the headline with a contrast structure naming the pain first, then your unique mechanism and benefits.
cards.use_when: When writing the supporting line under a headline on a landing page, PDP or ad landing page.

cards.title: Generate Headline Options with AI, Then Iterate Manually
cards.summary: Paste your existing page copy into an AI model, apply a direct-response headline prompt, and then refine the output rather than shipping it.
cards.use_when: When you are stuck writing hero copy for a product page or campaign page and need fast starting options.

cards.title: Above the Fold: Spend 80 to 90 Percent of Effort Here
cards.summary: The first screen is the only section every visitor sees, and roughly 60% never scroll past it, so start optimization there.
cards.use_when: When prioritizing a limited conversion optimization budget across a landing page or long product page.

cards.title: Progressive Disclosure for Lower-Friction Lead Capture
cards.summary: Ask for the simplest information first and reveal more complex fields only after the visitor engages.
cards.use_when: When designing lead forms, email or SMS capture, or a quiz-style entry point on a landing page or PDP.

cards.title: Strip the Landing Page Navigation to Conversion Actions Only
cards.summary: Remove external pages from the header and keep only the logo plus the actions you want clicked, sticky through the scroll.
cards.use_when: When building a campaign landing page or ad-specific page and deciding what belongs in the header.

cards.title: Benefit-Driven CTA Buttons for Product Pages
cards.summary: Make the primary product-page CTA visually dominant and frame the click around the shopper’s desired outcome rather than a generic action.
cards.use_when: Designing the main add-to-cart, bundle-selection, or campaign-page CTA for a physical product.

cards.title: Match the Product-Page Hero to Traffic Awareness
cards.summary: Lead with product selection for high-intent visitors, but lead with the problem, mechanism, and product relevance when campaign traffic is less aware.
cards.use_when: Choosing the above-the-fold structure for a PDP, collection landing page, or advertorial-to-product journey based on acquisition source and shopper intent.

cards.title: Use Pain–Agitate–Solution Ethically on Product Campaign Pages
cards.summary: For problem-aware shoppers, name the recognizable frustration, acknowledge failed alternatives, and present the product as a credible next step without exaggeration.
cards.use_when: Building a campaign landing page or advertorial-to-product journey for shoppers who recognize a problem but do not yet know which product category or brand to choose.

cards.title: Build Benefit-First Product Value Propositions
cards.summary: Translate product features into shopper outcomes by asking what each feature enables, then make the resulting benefit the section headline.
cards.use_when: Writing PDP benefit blocks, collection-page merchandising, product bundle descriptions, or campaign landing-page sections.

cards.title: Write PDP Headlines for Scanners
cards.summary: Assume many shoppers scan headings rather than read every paragraph, so every heading should communicate a standalone product benefit or decision aid.
cards.use_when: Writing product-page headings, campaign-page section titles, bundle descriptions, comparison blocks, and testimonial summaries.

cards.title: Create Scannable, Verifiable Social Proof
cards.summary: Use real reviews and customer stories in visible, varied formats, with accurate source attribution and summaries that let shoppers grasp the proof quickly.
cards.use_when: Adding reviews, UGC, case stories, or customer proof to a PDP, product landing page, bundle page, or cart-adjacent offer.

cards.title: Use Comparison Tables to Simplify Product Choice
cards.summary: Help shoppers evaluate a product, bundle, or category alternative with a factual, scannable comparison table rather than forcing them to infer differences from prose.
cards.use_when: Merchandising a flagship product against other formats, comparing bundles, or explaining how your product differs from a conventional alternative on a PDP or landing page.

cards.title: Show How the Product Fits Into the Customer Routine
cards.summary: Use a short three- or four-step how-it-works sequence that makes adoption feel clear and ends with the honest customer outcome.
cards.use_when: Explaining product setup, routine, replenishment, bundle usage, or a product-matching flow on a PDP or campaign landing page.
